primitives.verbatim_quote: Redesign A — time-stratified SR Protocol (reused from REPORT_WPA2_ROBUST): y = wpa2 clipped at stratum-train 99th pct, standardized on stratum-train; 9 W1 features standardized (StandardScaler fit on stratum-train); gplearn SymbolicRegressor, log-cosh fitness, function set {add,sub,mul,div,sqrt,log,abs,inv,tanh}, pop 2000 × 30 gens, parsimony 0.001.

primitives.name: Conditional Contribution Hypothesis
primitives.verbatim_quote: Inside the LATE stratum (all Q4/OT plays), quarter_seconds_remaining equals game seconds remaining, so the end-of-game time gradient is present in X4 exactly where the conditional-contribution hypothesis says it should matter.
primitives.assumptions: End-of-game time effects are concentrated in late quarters; temporal gradient is measurable through stratified regression.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When temporal proxy fails to distinguish strata (e.g., Q1 stratum has zero rows).

reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight hinges on the misalignment between `quarter_seconds_remaining` and game-level time, causing strata to collapse into degeneracy. This invalidates the intended temporal stratification, undermining the conditional contribution hypothesis. However, the LATE stratum still exhibits a meaningful time gradient, enabling empirical validation of the hypothesis through calibrated heuristics. The SR approach fails to recover the time term even under optimal conditions, indicating either a limitation in search space or a mismatch between the signal structure and symbolic representation. The residual gate reveals a thin, linear signal, suggesting that nonlinear discovery is constrained by data properties rather than algorithmic capability. The failure of SR to replicate the human time heuristic implies that the signal may be better captured by simpler models or requires more sophisticated regularization.
